title: Europe shows a better alternative to big SUVs at the Paris Auto Show
gist: At the Paris Auto Show, European brands including Citroen, VW Group, Audi, Fiat and Renault showed small, affordable EVs and adaptable designs, which the author argues contrast with big-SUV trends and Stellantis' US lineup. Most of these cars will not come to the United States.

insights.claim: Citroen says it will build its 2 CV concept within two years at a starting price of 15,000 euros ($16,766), positioned between microcars and superminis like the VW Polo.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: A sub-16k EV targets the affordability gap that has limited EV adoption.

insights.claim: VW Group says it has more than 150,000 orders for its Electric Urban Car Family, which includes the ID. Polo, ID. Cross, Cupra Raval and Skoda Epiq.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Order volume suggests real demand for affordable small EVs in Europe.

insights.claim: Audi's A2 e-tron is its most efficient car ever, with a WLTP rating of 12.8 kWh/100 km.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Efficiency over size is a European EV competitive axis.

insights.claim: The 2 CV concept's interior favors a stripped-back design with an 8-inch touchscreen and removable radio, in contrast to touchscreen overload.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Cost-cutting cabins can enable lower prices.

insights.claim: The author doubts that Citroen, Audi, Fiat or Renault concepts will reach the US, and contrasts Stellantis' European small cars with its US plan to relaunch a V8 Hellcat-powered Charger.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: The US market is structurally separate, favoring large vehicles, which limits benefits for European small-EV makers there.
insights.quote: I’m pretty sure none of the stuff you’re seeing here will come to the United States
insights.locator: But this article is meant to irritate you

insights.claim: The only electric minivan sold in the US is the VW ID. Buzz, which sold so poorly that VW suspended imports for a model year, suggesting low US odds for the Renault E-Space.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Weak US demand for EV people-carriers discourages launches.
insights.quote: There is a criminal lack of electric minivans on the market today

insights.claim: Fiat's Multiplay concept and Renault's E-Space concept offer adaptable alternatives to three-row SUVs, including a pickup conversion and a 'Petsenger' modular seat.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Modular EV design is a possible differentiator against SUVs.
insights.locator: What if I need something bigger?

insights.claim: Auto shows appear to be recovering as venues for debuts after years of brands pulling out and reveals moving offsite.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Return of reveals could change marketing spend toward trade shows.
insights.quote: Perhaps the days when auto shows debuted new models aren’t entirely over.
